findings.text: blocking: the change adds two keys to every candidate's rendered state, and the representative nine-candidate pick now estimates 2230 tokens against the test's ceiling of 2200 (gate-armed-head.log: 'assert 2230 <= 2200'). rendered_token_estimate is the picker's own production budget for the state it hands Jev, so the landed change puts a representative pick over that budget by 30 tokens; the two size bounds and the two field-set constants that assert this contract are in files the node was fenced out of, but the regression is caused by the landed change and the plan's done-when forbids any added failure in test files importing prompts.py.

blocking: the same two extra keys per candidate push the rendered state to 8086 characters against the bound 'assert len(rendered) <= 1500 * 5' (7500) at gate-armed-head.log: 'assert 8086 <= (1500 * 5)'. The comment above the bound says 'the bound still holds the whole prompt to a few KB', so the change breaches a declared prompt-size ceiling rather than a stale literal.

follow-on: test_rendered_state_is_one_json_object asserts 'set(payload["candidates"]["remote"]) == CANDIDATE_FIELDS' against a set literal declared at tests/test_jev_prompt_carries_what_it_weighs.py:43, so it reddens purely because the node's own output contract grew by moved_in and moved_off. The remedy is to add the two names to CANDIDATE_FIELDS; there is no production consequence, but the file is outside the node's write scope so the added failure stands.

follow-on: 'assert set(payload["candidates"]["clive"]) == CANDIDATE_KEYS' against the literal at tests/test_picker_return_time.py:31 reddens for the same reason; the length bound at line 273 passes, so this is the field-set contract and not the size bound the manifest's follow_ons attributes to it.

follow-on: the follow_ons line attributes all four added failures to size bounds ('the latter three bound the rendered state's size'), but gate-armed-head.log shows only two are size bounds (test_picker.py:262, test_picker_pressure.py:477) and the other two are exact-set field contracts (test_jev_prompt_carries_what_it_weighs.py:120, test_picker_return_time.py:274); it also records the base arm as showing 'zero failures through 79%', which is true but is not the summary-line comparison the done-when asks for, so the record reads as a completed two-arm comparison when one arm is incomplete.
